Sam K: afternoon spot-check — quick pipeline runthrough
Sam K: what I did: moved Kestrel to legal review, updated forecast to reflect slide-in ARR
Sam K: blockers: needs engineering confirmation on private deploy key handling + latency guarantees for on-prem setup
Sam K: today: follow up with SE + security, schedule customer sync if we get answers
Priya N: Kestrel asked for explicit customer-managed key control and an audit trail. They asked whether Redwood Private can do external key wrapping (their vendor uses a key-wrap-only flow). Eng folks — any quick yes/no? @Jorge (SE)
Jorge (SE): short: we support external KMS providers (AWS/GCP) and PKCS#11 HSMs in the on-prem package. External RMK-style key wrapping requires a config tweak but is supported. Example config snippet below:
Jorge (SE): ```yaml
kms_provider: external
key_wrap: pkcs11
pkcs11_lib: /usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so
wrap_policy: customer-managed
```
Jorge (SE): estimate: I can validate in a customer lab in ~1 business day. Need someone from infra to grant lab access.
Liam T: Kestrel also wants to know about model rollout behavior — specifically canary + auto-fallback to hosted if private fails. Is that documented for SOW language?
Sam K: not in the public playbook. Jorge, what's the runtime behavior and any perf implications if we mirror traffic for canarying?
Jorge (SE): runtime: you can configure canary % and a fallback model group. Two modes: mirrored (sync) and staged (async). Mirrored will add latency on the canary path; staged async has negligible latency impact. For SOW we can say: "supports percentage-based canarying with configurable fallback and two rollout modes (mirrored or staged)."
Priya N: Action items: Jorge -> validate the keywrap snippet + short one-pager for legal (by EOD). Liam -> draft canary SOW blurb and send to Sam. Sam -> schedule customer call for tomorrow 10am PT if Jorge validates by EOD.
